title: The press and the media
subtitle: sitcom, soap, tabloid, broadcast, set in
summary: Name the kinds of programme on TV and radio, describe tabloid and quality newspapers, and use the verbs that go with the media - broadcast, televise, shoot on location, set in, tweet.

lesson.heading: Kinds of TV and radio programme
rows: **talk show**
a show with a host and famous guests who answer questions about themselves
**cartoon**
a film where the characters are drawn rather than real
**game show**
a show where people compete to win prizes
**soap** (short for soap opera)
a series about the lives of a group of characters, broadcast every week over a long period
**documentary**
a programme investigating the facts about something
**sitcom**
a funny show where the same characters appear in a different story each week
**current affairs programme**
news about political events happening now
**detective drama**
a drama in which a crime is solved
lesson.note: The person who introduces a show is the **presenter**. One of the parts a story is divided into is an **episode**.

lesson.heading: The mass media
lesson.text: The **(mass) media** refers to TV, radio, newspapers and the Internet, i.e. **means** of communication which reach very large numbers of people.

examples.text: I'd like a job in the **media**, perhaps in TV or radio.
The Internet is an important **means** of communication.
examples.note: The noun means (a way of doing something) always ends in s, even in the singular.

lesson.heading: Watching and listening
lesson.text: **Subtitles** let you read what the characters are saying, perhaps in translation. If a film is **dubbed**, you hear the speech in your own language. To receive a lot of channels you may need a **satellite dish** on your roof or wall.

examples.text: Many channels depend on **commercials** to make money.
You can **stream** radio and TV broadcasts from the Internet.
**Catch-up TV**, or **TV on demand**, lets you watch programmes whenever you like.
A lot of stations offer free **podcasts** which you can **download**.

lesson.heading: Two kinds of newspaper

left.label: Popular / tabloid
left.text: Focuses on sensation rather than real news.
examples: **scandals** = events which shock people in a moral way

right.label: Quality
examples: complex political debate and long book reviews
**journalism** = collecting, writing and publishing or broadcasting news
**in-depth** = done carefully and in great detail

lesson.note: To read newspapers online you may have to **subscribe**, or pay a **subscription** - a sum of money paid regularly, e.g. once a year.

lesson.heading: Verbs connected with the media
rows: **broadcast**
The BBC World Service **broadcasts** throughout the world. (transmits TV/radio programmes)
**televise**
They're **televising** the opening of Parliament tomorrow. (less formal: showing)
**shoot / make on location**
The film was **shot on location** in Australia. (filmed in a real place, not a studio)
**be set in**
The series **is set in** London in the 1980s. (the place/time where the drama happens)
**tweet**
Within minutes, people were **tweeting** about it. (posting very short messages online)
**focus on**
The report **focused on** school meals. (emphasised, paid attention to)

lesson.text: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb: I have some news for you, and The news is on at 7 pm - never ~~a news~~ or ~~the news are~~.

exercises.prompt: What sort of TV programme is each person talking about?

pairs.left: It investigated how the banks had wasted billions of euros.
Walt Disney made a lot of them. Mickey Mouse was the most famous.
The Minister of Education was on it, discussing the new schools policy.
It's so funny, especially when the old uncle appears.
My mum watches it every day. She knows all the characters as if they were real.

exercises.prompt: What sort of programme is each person talking about?

pairs.left: We wanted to find out if it was going to rain tomorrow.
They always solve the murder in the end, but it's very exciting.
He interviewed that young star who just won an Oscar.
The prize is 500,000 pounds this week. That's a lot of money.
They showed a repeat of the Manchester United versus Valencia match.

exercises.prompt: I downloaded a great ___ about bees. I listened to it on my MP3 player in bed last night.
exercises.explanation: A podcast is an audio programme you download from the Internet.

exercises.prompt: I hate it when ___ interrupt a good film. I usually go and make a cup of tea while they're on.
exercises.explanation: Many channels depend on commercials to make money.

exercises.prompt: We've got a new satellite ___ on our roof. We can receive hundreds of channels now.
exercises.explanation: A satellite dish lets you receive many TV channels.

exercises.prompt: A lot of people use social networking sites as their main ___ of communication with their friends.
exercises.explanation: The noun means (a way of doing something) ends in s even in the singular.

exercises.prompt: With a fast broadband connection, you can ___ TV shows directly from the Internet.
exercises.explanation: You stream a broadcast rather than downloading the whole file first.

exercises.prompt: Which do you prefer if a film is in a foreign language, to read subtitles or to have the film ___?
exercises.explanation: If a film is dubbed, you hear the speech in your own language.

exercises.prompt: People often download ___ from the Internet so they don't need to watch them on the day they are transmitted.
exercises.explanation: Catch-up TV lets you watch broadcasts whenever you like.

exercises.prompt: Which newspaper would you expect each of these in?
The documentary ___ the food industry and focused on school meals.
exercises.explanation: To investigate is to try to find out the facts about something.

exercises.prompt: The programme was shot on ___ in Northern Finland.
exercises.explanation: Shot or made on location means filmed in a real place, not in a studio.

exercises.prompt: CNN ___ news programmes around the world.
exercises.explanation: To broadcast is to transmit TV or radio programmes.

exercises.prompt: They're ___ the cup final next week.
exercises.explanation: Televise is the more formal alternative to show.

exercises.prompt: The drama is ___ in Paris in the 1880s.
exercises.explanation: Be set in gives the place and time where a drama happens.

exercises.statement: I have a news for you about the cup final.
exercises.explanation: False - news is uncountable: I have some news for you.

exercises.answer: A quality newspaper focuses on serious journalism with in-depth articles.
exercises.explanation: Focus on means emphasise or pay attention to.
